did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah addressed the Jews living in Egypt in several places: Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph, and the land of Pathros.
Did you know? Jeremiah reminded the Jews in Egypt that they themselves had seen the destruction of Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which were left in ruins and without inhabitants.
Did you know? The LORD described the prophets as repeatedly sent to warn the people not to commit the detestable acts he hates.
Did you know? Jeremiah presented the continued worship of idols in Egypt as a danger to the entire family—men, women, children, and infants—until no remnant would be left.
Did you know? The people’s response to Jeremiah included men, women, and a large group of Jews living in Egypt; the women are specifically mentioned as those who burned incense to other gods.

Did you know? The people explicitly declared that they would continue burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, claiming that this was also what their ancestors, kings, and officials had done.
Did you know? Jeremiah responded to the people’s claim by saying that the LORD had not overlooked their incense and worship; he remembered them, and they had come to his mind.
Did you know? Jeremiah announced that only a few survivors of the sword would return from Egypt to Judah, and their return would prove that the word of the LORD had come true.
Did you know? The sign the LORD gave the Jews in Egypt was that the disaster he had spoken about would take place where they were, so they would know that his words had come true.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, Pharaoh Hophra is mentioned, and the LORD announces that he will be handed over to his enemies, just as Zedekiah king of Judah was handed over to Nebuchadnezzar.
